messages:
ella.sre: FYI seeing intermittent NCCL hangs on a 16-GPU job in eu-west-2. Correlates with packet drops on the east-west path between rack-5 and rack-6 when MTU=9000.
ana.infra: Can you paste the nic counters and any mlx5 logs?
ella.sre: quick dump below — logs from node gnode-5 around 12:14 UTC.
ella.sre: ```
Dec 03 12:14:07 gnode-5 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: rq_overflow: RQ overrun on port 1
Dec 03 12:14:07 gnode-5 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_core: DROP rx_csum_err=12 rx_vlan_err=0 rx_dropped=48
Dec 03 12:14:08 gnode-5 nvidia-gpudirect: mr_reg: EFAULT during registration
```
mike.runtime: mr_reg EFAULT + mlx5 RQ overrun screams packet reassembly / offload mismatch. Do you see different ethtool -k between the two hosts?
ella.sre: yes — gnode-5 reports GSO: on, GRO: on; gnode-6 had GRO off after a recent kernel tweak. I flipped GRO back on gnode-6 and reran — still saw occasional drops.
kai.ml: Could be fragmentation across TOR due to PMTU differences or vxlan offload not matching. Are we using RoCEv2 over L3 or pinned IB fabrics?
ella.sre: RoCEv2 over L3, routed between ToRs with ECMP. PMTU on the path sometimes falls to 1500 because one TOR has vxlan offload disabled on a few ports.
nana.infra: Oof. That would cause a mismatch: NICs sending 9000-byte segments with GSO, TOR strips or fragments -> kernel sees bad checksums / RQ overflow.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot reported topology change on tor-sw-2 at 12:05 UTC (port flap, upgrade).
nana.infra: Can you run these on both nodes and paste outputs?
nana.infra: ```
# on gnode-5 && gnode-6
ethtool -k eth0
ip link show dev eth0
ip route get 10.0.42.1
ibv_devinfo -v
```
ella.sre: Ran them — differences: gnode-6 had tx-checksum offload on, but rx-checksum offload off in kernel due to a late firmware->driver change. Also got mtu path discovery showing 1500 on one hop.
mike.runtime: For immediate mitigation, drop MTU to 1500 on all nodes in that rack and force GRO/GSO off for a few minutes to see if NCCL stabilizes. We don't want reassembly happening in TOR.
kai.ml: Also collect perf counters during run: `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and `ibv_rc_pingpong -F -d mlx5_0` to check RNR/NAK rates.
ella.sre: Did a controlled test: 1500 MTU + GRO/GSO off -> run stable for 30m, no NCCL hang, rx_dropped went to zero. Reverted to 9000+GSO and hang returned within 6m.
nana.infra: Sounds like path MTU inconsistency + offload heterogeneity. Long term fix: coordinate TOR firmware and vxlan/geneve offload settings, push consistent netdev offload config via ansible, and add an eBPF check in preflight to assert PMTU across ToRs for RoCE routes.
mike.runtime: Also schedule NIC firmware updates on the problematic ToR-facing ports — mlx5 FW had a known bug with large GSO segments + ECMP that was fixed in 2023-11.
oncall-bot: @ana.infra created ticket INF-4823 linking ToR fw and host offload mismatch (priority P1).
nana.infra: I'll own rollout plan. Action items: 1) run ansible change to set mtu=9000 + consistent offloads or drop to 1500 depending on ToR FW timeline, 2) add PMTU e2e check in infra CI, 3) patch NCCL job config to gate-large-mtu on known rack list.
kai.ml: Add a runtime guard to fall back to TCP NCCL collective on repeated mr_reg errors — that will keep jobs alive while infra fixes propagate.
ella.sre: Thanks all. I'll attach packet captures from both sides (pcap + ibtrace) in the ticket. For now, keeping affected racks at 1500 and rolling through NIC fw next week. :thumbsup:
